candidates.raw_excerpt: Slipping ratings, a revolving door of lead actors, and nothing quite hitting like that old school David Tennant run. It’s dog days for “Doctor Who” fans, whose lives aren’t likely to be made any better by the prospect of AI creeping into the show. While speaking at the Royal Television Society conference in London, BBC director Matt Brittin extolled the amazing efficiency of using AI to crank out footage — before raising the possibility of using it on one of the British broadcaster’s most beloved series. “Everyone’s got the ability in their hands — or six billion people have — to create content at the standard of a Hollywood studio,” Brittin said, as quoted by Variety . “Somebody sent me a 50-minute episode of ‘Doctor Who’ that was AI-generated the other day. It’s pretty good,” he continued. “I mean, it’s not going to replace humans, and we’ll come on to that. So everyone’s a creator.” Brittin, it’s worth noting, was president of Europe, Middle East, and Africa operations at Google — a major purveyor of AI tech — before joining the BBC . You have to wonder what Brittin’s idea of “pretty good” is. Attempts at using AI to crank out a movie or short film have invariably produced low grade slop . While the tech can sometimes create realistic images or scenes in isolation, cobbling together disparate, screensaver-worthy images together doesn’t constitute an episode of hit television. candidates.title: Pacific Island Fisheries; Annual Catch Limit and Accountability Measures for Mariana Bottomfish Management Unit Species in the Guam Management Subarea
candidates.raw_excerpt: NMFS is modifying the annual catch limit (ACL) and accountability measures (AM) for Mariana bottomfish management unit species (MUS) in the Guam Management Subarea (the fishery). The rule increases the ACL from 31,000 pounds (lb) (14,061 kilograms (kg)) to 34,500 lb (15,649 kg), replaces the in-season AM with a post-season overage adjustment if the average catch from the most recent 3 years exceeds the ACL, and removes the higher performance standard that closes the fishery in Federal waters for any overage. This EFP would exempt one catcher/processor vessel from complying with regulations that prohibit the retention of Pacific halibut and donation of Pacific halibut prohibited species. candidates.title: Airworthiness Directives; Leonardo S.p.a. Helicopters

This AD was prompted by a report of a nozzle exhaust duct clamp separating from the engine nozzle duct and coming to rest on the tail rotor (TR) drive shaft. This AD requires repetitively inspecting certain clamp assemblies and, depending on the results of the inspection, replacing parts. This AD also prohibits the installation of an affected clamp assembly, unless certain requirements are met. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

candidates.title: Airworthiness Directives; The Boeing Company Airplanes
candidates.raw_excerpt: The FAA is adopting a new airworthiness directive (AD) for all The Boeing Company Model 757-300 series airplanes. This AD was prompted by a crack growth analysis that indicated that existing maintenance planning data (MPD) and supplemental structural inspection program (SSIP) tasks do not provide adequate inspection opportunities to detect cracks in the upper frames around the uppermost fastener common to the fail-safe chord at the fuselage frame splices. This AD requires an inspection or maintenance record check for existing repairs, repetitive inspections of the upper frames around the uppermost fastener common to the fail-safe chord at the fuselage frame splices for any cracks, and applicable on-condition actions. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

candidates.title: Airworthiness Directives; Airbus Helicopters
candidates.raw_excerpt: The FAA is adopting a new airworthiness directive (AD) for all Airbus Helicopters Model AS355E, AS355F, AS355F1, AS355F2, and AS355N helicopters. This AD was prompted by the determination that the tail rotor drive fan wheels (fan wheels) and the impeller second stage have been incorrectly identified during production. This AD requires verifying the serial number and amendment of the log cards of the affected parts, and depending on the findings, performing a one-time borescope inspection to verify consistency between the log cards and the affected parts. Depending on the results of the inspection, this AD requires replacing or re-identifying certain parts. candidates.title: Trusted Computing Group Creates Key New Working Group Focusing on Aerospace Security
candidates.raw_excerpt: The Trusted Computing Group (TCG) has created a new Aerospace and Non-Terrestrial Systems Solutions Working Group (AERO-SWG) as it looks to play a key role in keeping satellite systems secure. Focusing on satellite networks, unmanned systems, autonomous platforms, and disconnected edge environments, AERO-SWG will aim to help operators apply trusted computing principles to strengthen the resilience and integrity of the systems now central to global communications and critical infrastructure. TCG announced the new group, Sept. 29. AERO-SWG will aim to establish trust within the devices, platforms, gateways, and supply chains that underpin the global communications, defense, transportation, and critical infrastructure society now relies upon. This will be achieved through practical guidance, gap analysis, and recommendations to existing TCG Work Groups. The group will be chaired by TCG member Thorsten Stremlau of Nvidia. AERO-SWG will explore how layered hardware and firmware security can be applied across aircraft, satellites and ground stations to strengthen trust at the platform level. This includes Trusted Platform Modile (TPM)-based Roots-of-Trust for flight-critical software, Device Identifier Composition Engine (DICE) for lightweight subsystem protection, and CyRes for restoring corrupted firmware in flight or in orbit. “AERO-SWG gives the industry a dedicated forum to ensure trusted computing in the toughest aerospace environments, including satellites and autonomous systems. By bringing experts together to focus on practical needs and real deployment barriers, the group will help accelerate the development of secure and interoperable technologies in this crucial sector,” Joe Pennisi, president of TCG, said in a statement. As with most missions to the ISS, Crew-13 requires an instantaneous launch window, currently scheduled for 11:10 AM EDT (15:10 UTC). Crew Dragon Grace (C213) will be on its second flight, having previously flown the Axiom-4 mission to the ISS. Grace is scheduled to deliver four astronauts to the Station, with the vehicle docking to the Harmony forward port at 8:00 PM EDT on Oct. 1. NASA astronaut and commander Jessica Watkins will be on her second spaceflight, with NASA astronaut and pilot Luke Delaney flying on his first mission. Mission Specialists Joshua Kutryk from the Canadian Space Agency (CSA) and Sergey Teteryatnikov (Roscosmos) are also first-time flyers. candidates.raw_excerpt: Artemis Accords signatories will meet at the International Astronautical Congress next week to discuss concrete ways countries can work together on responsible operations in space, according to a NASA release. The Artemis Accords Principals’ Meeting in Turkey will be led by NASA Deputy Administrator Matt Anderson and Maj. Gen. Roberto Melgar Sheen, director of the Peruvian Space Agency. The meeting will focus on two initiatives: How space-faring nations can support countries wanting to establish or grow their presence in orbit; How to distribute recommendations on mitigating lunar debris. The more the merrier: The meeting comes as the group of Artemis Accords nations grew to 76 countries, with the additions of Albania, Croatia, Côte d’Ivoire, and San Marino last week. The recent influx has helped the partnership hit a few milestones, according to NASA. 40% of global countries are now signed onto the non-binding agreement; About two-thirds of signatories to the 1967 Outer Space Treaty have also signed the Artemis Accords; Nearly one-third of the signatories of the accords have joined since President Donald Trump took office for the second time in January 2025. “You’ve got the Italian Space Agency contributing a habitat that will put astronauts on the Moon. JAXA is making big contributions,” Isaacman said last week at Payload’s Off World event in Houston. “At least half of the Artemis Accords signatories have made commitments for some sort of scientific or tech demonstration payload that’s going to go to the lunar surface.” The big picture: 16 nations have joined since we published our analysis last year, so this seemed as good a time as any to update our charts and graphics. We’ll start with our world map of signatories. 2026 has been a banner year for the accords, adding 17 signatories. It’s the biggest year for the accords since 2024, which added 19 new nations.
